meta.name: Billing service
meta.description: Customers view and pay invoices in a React SPA. An nginx gateway terminates TLS and proxies to a FastAPI service that stores invoices in Postgres, charges cards through Stripe and queues receipt jobs in Redis for a worker that emails receipts via SendGrid. Users authenticate with Auth0.
meta.assumptions: Derived from docker-compose.yml and source code. The backend network is internal-only (docker-compose.yml:31). Auth0, Stripe and SendGrid are trusted third parties outside our control.

threatTypes.title: Spoofing the {source.Name} process
threatTypes.description: An attacker can impersonate {source.Name} when talking to {target.Name} across a trust boundary, and gain access that {target.Name} only means to give {source.Name}.
threatTypes.mitigation: Authenticate the calling process with a standard mechanism such as mutual TLS, signed tokens or OS-level service identities, and verify that identity on {target.Name}.
threatTypes.include: source is 'GE.P' and (target is 'GE.P' or target is 'GE.DS') and (flow crosses 'GE.TB.L' or flow crosses 'GE.TB.B')

threatTypes.title: Spoofing the {target.Name} process
threatTypes.description: {source.Name} cannot tell whether it is really talking to {target.Name}. An attacker who stands up a look-alike endpoint can collect the data sent over {flow.Name} or return malicious responses.
threatTypes.mitigation: Authenticate the destination, for example with TLS server certificates validated against a trusted root, certificate pinning or mutual authentication.
threatTypes.include: (source is 'GE.P' or source is 'GE.EI' or source is 'GE.DS') and target is 'GE.P' and (flow crosses 'GE.TB.L' or flow crosses 'GE.TB.B')

threatTypes.title: Spoofing the {source.Name} external entity
threatTypes.description: An attacker can pose as {source.Name} and send requests to {target.Name} on its behalf.
threatTypes.mitigation: Require {source.Name} to authenticate (strong passwords plus MFA for people; client certificates, signed tokens or API keys with rotation for systems).
threatTypes.include: source is 'GE.EI' and target is 'GE.P'

threatTypes.title: Spoofing of source data store {source.Name}
threatTypes.description: If an attacker can replace or impersonate {source.Name}, {target.Name} will trust and process data the attacker controls.
threatTypes.mitigation: Authenticate the data store connection and protect where its location comes from (configuration, DNS, file paths), so that it cannot be redirected.
threatTypes.include: source is 'GE.DS'

threatTypes.title: Spoofing of destination data store {target.Name}
threatTypes.description: If an attacker can impersonate {target.Name}, data that {source.Name} writes may go to a location the attacker controls.
threatTypes.mitigation: Authenticate the data store and lock down the configuration that names it. Use least-privilege credentials scoped to that store.
threatTypes.include: target is 'GE.DS'

threatTypes.title: Spoofing of the {target.Name} external destination entity
threatTypes.description: An attacker can impersonate {target.Name} and receive data that {source.Name} meant only for that entity.
threatTypes.mitigation: Verify the identity of {target.Name} before sending data, for example by validating its TLS certificate, pinning the certificate or using signed callbacks.
threatTypes.include: source is 'GE.P' and target is 'GE.EI' and (flow crosses 'GE.TB.L' or flow crosses 'GE.TB.B')

threatTypes.title: Potential lack of input validation for {target.Name}
threatTypes.description: Data arriving at {target.Name} over {flow.Name} can be changed in transit. Input that is not validated can lead to denial of service, elevation of privilege or information disclosure in {target.Name}.
threatTypes.mitigation: Validate all input against an allow-list (type, length, format, range) at the boundary and reject anything that does not match. Protect the channel with TLS.
threatTypes.include: (source is 'GE.P' or source is 'GE.EI') and target is 'GE.P' and (flow crosses 'GE.TB.L' or flow crosses 'GE.TB.B')

threatTypes.title: {source.Name} process memory tampered
threatTypes.description: {target.Name} runs unmanaged code. Memory-corruption bugs reachable from {source.Name} could let an attacker change process memory and hijack execution.
threatTypes.mitigation: Use memory-safe languages where possible and enable compiler and OS mitigations (ASLR, DEP/NX, CFG, stack protectors). Fuzz the input parsers.
threatTypes.include: source is 'GE.P' and target is 'GE.P' and target.codeType is 'Unmanaged'

threatTypes.title: Replay attacks
threatTypes.description: The custom protocol between {source.Name} and {target.Name} may accept captured messages replayed by an attacker.
threatTypes.mitigation: Include nonces, timestamps or sequence numbers in authenticated messages and reject duplicates or stale messages.
threatTypes.include: source is 'GE.P' and target is 'GE.P' and source.implementsCommunicationProtocol is 'Yes'

threatTypes.title: Collision attacks
threatTypes.description: If the protocol between {source.Name} and {target.Name} relies on weak hashes, an attacker can craft colliding messages that pass integrity checks.
threatTypes.mitigation: Use modern collision-resistant algorithms (SHA-256 or better, HMAC) and avoid MD5 and SHA-1 for integrity.
threatTypes.include: source is 'GE.P' and target is 'GE.P' and source.implementsCommunicationProtocol is 'Yes'

threatTypes.title: Risks from logging
threatTypes.description: An attacker can inject log entries or tamper with existing logs, which can corrupt log viewers or hide their activity.
threatTypes.mitigation: Encode or neutralize log input, write logs append-only, and send them to a separate, access-controlled log store.
threatTypes.include: (source is 'GE.P' and target is 'GE.DS' and target.storesLogData is 'Yes') or (target is 'GE.P' and source is 'GE.DS' and source.storesLogData is 'Yes')

threatTypes.title: Authenticated data flow compromised
threatTypes.description: {flow.Name} is authenticated but its contents are not fully protected, so an attacker on the path can read or change the data after authentication.
threatTypes.mitigation: Protect the channel end to end with confidentiality and integrity, for example TLS 1.2+ with strong cipher suites.
threatTypes.include: (flow.authenticatesSource is 'Yes' or flow.authenticatesDestination is 'Yes')

threatTypes.title: Potential SQL injection vulnerability for {target.Name}
threatTypes.description: If {source.Name} builds queries from untrusted input, an attacker can run arbitrary SQL against {target.Name}.
threatTypes.mitigation: Use parameterized queries or prepared statements for all database access. Grant the database account only the permissions it needs.
threatTypes.include: (target is 'SE.DS.TMCore.SQL' and source is 'GE.P')

threatTypes.title: Possible SQL injection vulnerability for {target.Name}
threatTypes.description: An external entity talks to the SQL database {target.Name} directly, so any query it can influence is open to injection.
threatTypes.mitigation: Put a process in front of the database that validates requests and uses parameterized queries. Do not expose the database directly.
threatTypes.include: (target is 'SE.DS.TMCore.SQL' and source is 'GE.EI')

threatTypes.title: XML DTD and XSLT processing
threatTypes.description: {target.Name} parses XML from {flow.Name}. DTDs, external entities or XSLT can enable XXE, file disclosure, SSRF or billion-laughs denial of service.
threatTypes.mitigation: Disable DTD processing and external entity resolution in the XML parser, and never run XSLT from untrusted sources.
threatTypes.include: (flow.XMLenc is 'Yes' and target is 'GE.P')

threatTypes.title: JavaScript Object Notation processing
threatTypes.description: {target.Name} parses JSON from {flow.Name}. Unsafe parsing, deserialization to arbitrary types or prototype pollution can let an attacker run code or corrupt data.
threatTypes.mitigation: Parse with a strict JSON parser (never eval), validate against a schema, and do not deserialize into polymorphic or arbitrary types.
threatTypes.include: ((flow is 'SE.DF.TMCore.HTTP' or flow is 'SE.DF.TMCore.HTTPS') and flow.JSON is 'Yes' and target is 'GE.P')

threatTypes.title: Cross site scripting
threatTypes.description: {target.Name} may reflect untrusted input into pages without encoding it, which lets an attacker run script in other users' browsers.
threatTypes.mitigation: Encode output for its context (HTML, attribute, JS, URL), validate input, and deploy a strict Content Security Policy.
threatTypes.include: (target is 'SE.P.TMCore.WebServer' or target is 'SE.P.TMCore.WebApp')

threatTypes.title: Persistent cross site scripting
threatTypes.description: Content stored in {source.Name} may contain script that {target.Name} later renders for other users.
threatTypes.mitigation: Encode stored content when rendering it, sanitize rich text with a vetted library, and use a Content Security Policy.
threatTypes.include: (target is 'SE.P.TMCore.WebServer' or target is 'SE.P.TMCore.WebApp') and source is 'GE.DS'

threatTypes.title: The {target.Name} data store could be corrupted
threatTypes.description: Data written to {target.Name} across a trust boundary can be changed in transit or written by an unauthorized party, which corrupts the store.
threatTypes.mitigation: Authenticate and authorize every write, protect the channel, validate data before storing it, and keep tested backups.
threatTypes.include: (source is 'GE.P' or source is 'GE.EI') and target is 'GE.DS' and (flow crosses 'GE.TB.L' or flow crosses 'GE.TB.B')

threatTypes.title: Lower trusted subject updates logs
threatTypes.description: If less-trusted subjects can write to the log store {target.Name}, an attacker can forge or erase entries, and the logs can no longer be used as evidence.
threatTypes.mitigation: Separate log writers by trust level, make logs append-only, and authenticate every writer.
threatTypes.include: (source is 'GE.P' or source is 'GE.EI') and (target is 'GE.DS') and (target.storesLogData is 'Yes')

threatTypes.title: Data logs from an unknown source
threatTypes.description: {target.Name} may accept log data without recording who sent it, so entries cannot be traced to an accountable source.
threatTypes.mitigation: Authenticate log producers and record the producer identity with each entry.
threatTypes.include: (source is 'GE.P' or source is 'GE.EI') and (target is 'GE.DS') and (target.storesLogData is 'Yes')

threatTypes.title: Insufficient auditing
threatTypes.description: If {source.Name} does not log security-relevant events (logins, privilege changes, data access) to {target.Name}, incidents cannot be detected or investigated.
threatTypes.mitigation: Define which security events must be logged, include actor, action, target and time, and alert on suspicious patterns.
threatTypes.include: source is 'GE.P' and target is 'GE.DS' and target.storesLogData is 'Yes'

threatTypes.title: Potential weak protections for audit data
threatTypes.description: Audit data in {target.Name} may be readable or changeable by too many principals, which puts its integrity and confidentiality at risk.
threatTypes.mitigation: Restrict access to audit data, sign or hash-chain entries, and keep audit logs in a separate security domain.
threatTypes.include: source is 'GE.P' and target is 'GE.DS' and target.storesLogData is 'Yes'

threatTypes.title: Potential data repudiation by {target.Name}
threatTypes.description: {target.Name} may later deny having received or acted on data from {source.Name}, because nothing records the transaction.
threatTypes.mitigation: Log receipt of security-relevant requests with timestamps and request identifiers. Consider signed receipts for high-value transactions.
threatTypes.include: target is 'GE.P' and (flow crosses 'GE.TB.L' or flow crosses 'GE.TB.B')

threatTypes.title: External entity {target.Name} potentially denies receiving data
threatTypes.description: {target.Name} can claim it never received data from {source.Name}.
threatTypes.mitigation: Record delivery and acknowledgement of important messages, for example with signed acknowledgements or delivery receipts.
threatTypes.include: target is 'GE.EI' and (flow crosses 'GE.TB.L' or flow crosses 'GE.TB.B')

threatTypes.title: Data store denies {source.Name} potentially writing data
threatTypes.description: There may be no proof that {source.Name} wrote a given record to {target.Name}.
threatTypes.mitigation: Record the writer identity and time with each write, and keep change history or audit tables for important data.
threatTypes.include: target is 'GE.DS' and (flow crosses 'GE.TB.L' or flow crosses 'GE.TB.B')

threatTypes.title: Authorization bypass
threatTypes.description: {source.Name} uses its own authorization logic for {target.Name}. Flaws in that logic, or paths that skip it, can expose data to unauthorized users.
threatTypes.mitigation: Check authorization server-side on every request, deny by default, and add tests for every role and resource combination.
threatTypes.include: source is 'GE.P' and target is 'GE.DS' and source.implementsCustomAuthorizationMechanism is 'Yes'

threatTypes.title: Data flow sniffing
threatTypes.description: Data on {flow.Name} crosses a trust boundary without encryption, so anyone on the network path can read it.
threatTypes.mitigation: Encrypt the channel (TLS 1.2+, IPsec) and do not send sensitive data that the receiver does not need.
threatTypes.include: ((source is 'GE.P' or source is 'GE.EI') and target is 'GE.P' and (flow crosses 'GE.TB.L' or flow crosses 'GE.TB.B')) or (source is 'GE.P' and target is 'GE.DS' and (flow crosses 'GE.TB.L' or flow crosses 'GE.TB.B'))

threatTypes.title: Weak access control for a resource
threatTypes.description: If the access control on {source.Name} is too permissive, data can be read by principals other than {target.Name}.
threatTypes.mitigation: Apply least-privilege access control lists to the data store and review who can read it.
threatTypes.include: source is 'GE.DS' and (target is 'GE.P' or target is 'GE.EI')

threatTypes.title: Weak credential storage
threatTypes.description: Credentials stored in {target.Name} may be readable or recoverable if the store is compromised.
threatTypes.mitigation: Store passwords as salted hashes from an adaptive algorithm (Argon2id, scrypt, bcrypt), and keep secrets in a dedicated vault or HSM.
threatTypes.include: source is 'GE.P' and target is 'GE.DS' and target.storesCredentials is 'Yes'

threatTypes.title: Weak credential transit
threatTypes.description: Credentials sent over {flow.Name} between machines may be exposed in transit.
threatTypes.mitigation: Send credentials only over an encrypted, server-authenticated channel, and prefer token-based or challenge-response authentication.
threatTypes.include: source is 'GE.P' and (target is 'GE.P' or target is 'GE.DS') and (flow crosses 'SE.TB.L.TMCore.Machine')

threatTypes.title: Weak authentication scheme
threatTypes.description: A custom or weak authentication scheme between {source.Name} and {target.Name} may be open to brute force, credential theft or bypass.
threatTypes.mitigation: Use well-reviewed standard protocols (OAuth 2.1/OIDC, Kerberos, mutual TLS) rather than custom schemes, and enforce rate limiting and MFA where it applies.
threatTypes.include: source is 'GE.P' and target is 'GE.P' and source.implementsAuthenticationScheme is 'Yes'

threatTypes.title: Potential excessive resource consumption for {source.Name} or {target.Name}
threatTypes.description: Requests from {source.Name} to {target.Name} could use up CPU, memory, connections or storage and degrade service.
threatTypes.mitigation: Set quotas, timeouts and connection pool limits, paginate queries, and monitor resource use.
threatTypes.include: source is 'GE.P' and target is 'GE.DS'

threatTypes.title: Potential process crash or stop for {target.Name}
threatTypes.description: Malformed or excessive input from {source.Name} could crash {target.Name} or make it stop responding.
threatTypes.mitigation: Validate input, handle errors without crashing, apply rate limiting, and run the process under a supervisor that restarts it.
threatTypes.include: target is 'GE.P' and (flow crosses 'GE.TB.L' or flow crosses 'GE.TB.B')

threatTypes.title: Data flow {flow.Name} is potentially interrupted
threatTypes.description: An attacker on the path can block or drop traffic on {flow.Name}, so {target.Name} never receives the data.
threatTypes.mitigation: Design for retries and timeouts, use redundant paths where availability matters, and monitor the flow.
threatTypes.include: (flow crosses 'GE.TB.L' or flow crosses 'GE.TB.B')

threatTypes.title: Data store inaccessible
threatTypes.description: An attacker can make the data store unreachable across the trust boundary, which leaves dependent processes without their data.
threatTypes.mitigation: Provide redundancy and failover for the store, protect its network path, and degrade gracefully when it is unavailable.
threatTypes.include: (source is 'GE.DS' or target is 'GE.DS') and (flow crosses 'GE.TB.L' or flow crosses 'GE.TB.B')

threatTypes.title: Weakness in SSO authorization
threatTypes.description: Weak integration with the identity provider {target.Name} (token validation, redirect handling, scope checks) can let an attacker gain access they were not granted.
threatTypes.mitigation: Validate token signature, issuer, audience and expiry; use exact redirect URIs; use PKCE and state; and grant only the scopes each client needs.
threatTypes.include: target is 'SE.EI.TMCore.AuthProvider'

threatTypes.title: Elevation using impersonation
threatTypes.description: {source.Name} may be able to make {target.Name} act with its own privileges or another principal's, for example through confused-deputy calls or impersonation.
threatTypes.mitigation: Carry the caller's identity through calls, authorize on behalf of the original caller, and run {target.Name} with least privilege.
threatTypes.include: (source is 'GE.EI' or source is 'GE.P') and target is 'GE.P'

threatTypes.title: {target.Name} may be subject to elevation of privilege using remote code execution
threatTypes.description: If {source.Name} can trigger code execution in {target.Name} (injection, deserialization, memory corruption), it gains {target.Name}'s privileges.
threatTypes.mitigation: Remove dangerous sinks (eval, shell, unsafe deserialization), validate input, sandbox the process and run it with least privilege.
threatTypes.include: target is 'GE.P' and (flow crosses 'GE.TB.L' or flow crosses 'GE.TB.B')

threatTypes.title: Elevation by changing the execution flow in {target.Name}
threatTypes.description: Input from {source.Name} might change how {target.Name} runs, for example by skipping checks or selecting privileged code paths.
threatTypes.mitigation: Validate every control input, check state transitions server-side, and do not let client-supplied data select code paths.
threatTypes.include: target is 'GE.P' and (flow crosses 'GE.TB.L' or flow crosses 'GE.TB.B')

threatTypes.title: Cross site request forgery
threatTypes.description: A malicious site can make a user's browser send authenticated requests over {flow.Name} to {target.Name} without the user's intent, because the request carries no unpredictable token.
threatTypes.mitigation: Require anti-forgery tokens or same-site cookies (SameSite=Lax/Strict), check the Origin/Referer headers, and require re-authentication for sensitive actions.
threatTypes.include: (source is 'GE.P' or source is 'GE.EI') and (target is 'GE.P') and (flow.authenticatesSource is 'Not Selected' or flow.authenticatesSource is 'Yes') and (flow.54851a3b-65da-4902-b4e0-94ef015be735 is 'None' or flow.54851a3b-65da-4902-b4e0-94ef015be735 is 'Not Selected') and (flow crosses 'GE.TB.L' or flow crosses 'GE.TB.B')
threatTypes.exclude: (source is 'SE.P.TMCore.OSProcess' or source is 'SE.P.TMCore.Thread' or source is 'SE.P.TMCore.KernelThread' or source is 'SE.P.TMCore.WinApp' or source is 'SE.P.TMCore.NetApp' or source is 'SE.P.TMCore.WebServer' or source is 'SE.P.TMCore.Win32Service' or source is 'SE.P.TMCore.WebSvc' or source is 'SE.P.TMCore.VM' or (source is 'SE.P.TMCore.Modern' and source.internetClientServer is 'No' and source.internetClient is 'No') or source is 'SE.EI.TMCore.AuthProvider' or source is 'SE.EI.TMCore.WebSvc' or source is 'SE.EI.TMCore.WebApp' or source is 'SE.EI.TMCore.Megasevrice' or source is 'SE.EI.TMCore.CRT' or source is 'SE.EI.TMCore.NFX' or source is 'SE.EI.TMCore.WinRT') or (target is 'SE.P.TMCore.ThickClient' or target is 'SE.P.TMCore.BrowserClient' or target is 'SE.P.TMCore.PlugIn' or target is 'SE.P.TMCore.Modern') or (flow crosses 'SE.TB.L.TMCore.Machine' or flow crosses 'SE.TB.L.TMCore.Kernel' or flow crosses 'SE.TB.L.TMCore.AppContainer' or flow crosses 'SE.TB.B.TMCore.CorpNet' or flow crosses 'SE.TB.B.TMCore.Sandbox')

threats.description: If less-trusted subjects can write to the log store Audit log, an attacker can forge or erase entries, and the logs can no longer be used as evidence.
threats.mitigation: Separate log writers by trust level, make logs append-only, and authenticate every writer.
